title: Peculiar galaxy NGC 3256
caption: The peculiar galaxy NGC 3256, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 3256 · constellation Vela · about 100 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Ranked #81 on ESA/Hubble’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: This Hubble picture shows the peculiar galaxy NGC 3256, about 100 million light-years from Earth in the constellation Vela. Its distorted appearance is the legacy of a past galactic merger.

Mergers can stir up and compress the gas inside galaxies, and that can set off a starburst, a period of unusually intense star formation. Because its own merger has already happened, NGC 3256 is an ideal place to investigate starbursts that were triggered by galaxies coming together.

The image combines observations from two of Hubble's cameras, Wide Field Camera 3 and the Advanced Camera for Surveys, including filters that isolate light from glowing gas. An earlier Hubble image of NGC 3256 was released as part of a collection of interacting galaxies assembled for the telescope's 18th birthday, and this newer view revisits the same restless object.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.29 x 3.31 arcminutes) and distance (100 million light years), the frame spans roughly 96,000 × 96,000 light-years. Its light set out about 100 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble's WFC3 and ACS observed in visible and near-infrared light, including filters for hydrogen and sulphur emission; the colour mapping isn't published.
